Subject: Initial redlines and SOW questions for the SummitForge connector

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the teams are excited about the connector. Our legal team attached a first-pass set of redlines for the MSA and DPA and flagged a couple of items in the SOW we want clarified before we proceed to procurement. High-level items they care about:

- Data residency & subprocessing: require explicit vendor list and subprocessor notification window.
- Indemnity cap clarification tied to fees.
- Audit scope for security assessments (SOC2 vs custom questionnaires).

I attached SummitForge_Redlines_v3.pdf and a markup of the SOW (Connector_SOW_draft_v2.docx). Any chance you can share Redwood's standard positions and call out items you cannot accept? We have a tight target to finalize by 8/30 to align with our Q4 roadmap.

Quick ask: can we get a short call with your legal/procurement folks Wednesday afternoon PT?

Thanks,
Ethan Brooks
Head of Platform Partnerships
SummitForge

Ethan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear priorities. Looping in Sergio (legal) and Laura (procurement) from Redwood so we can triage items quickly. Preliminary notes below; Sergio and Laura — please review the attached redlines and confirm positions.

Quick responses to your bullets:
- Data residency / subprocessors: we publish our subprocessor list and can agree to a 30-day notification window for material additions. For controlled/private deployments we can support region-specific hosting (we can add this to SOW).
- Indemnity cap: our standard position ties cap to 12 months of fees unless there's gross negligence; Sergio — can you comment on carveouts?
- Audit scope: SOC 2 is our baseline; for customer-specific audits we typically offer questionnaire responses and a scoped on-site or remote audit at cost.

We can do a 30-min alignment call Wednesday 8/25 at 2:00pm PT — does that work for your team? If so I’ll send a calendar invite and attach a summarized exception log so we can focus on the 5-7 sticking points.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Alliances Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested positions on SummitForge redlines

Tessa / Laura —

I reviewed SummitForge_Redlines_v3.pdf. High-level suggested positions below (keeps us commercially reasonable while protecting core exposure):

1) Indemnity / cap: propose counter of 12 months fees with carveouts for wilful misconduct and IP infringement. Push back on broad indemnities tied to downstream customer claims.
2) Subprocessors: agree to publish list and 30-day notice. Reject requirement to obtain prior written consent for routine cloud providers; accept prior notice + objection right for new analytics vendors.
3) Data retention & deletion: keep our standard retention table but add SOW appendix to specify retention for connector logs (default 90 days, option to extend via paid add-on).
4) Audit scope: provide SOC2 + questionnaire. Offer a limited remote evidence review for any material concerns. Avoid unlimited onsite audits; if insisted, charge for incremental costs.

I prepared a short exceptions log (attached to my internal note). Laura — procurement will need to confirm if we can accept their proposed payment terms (45 days) or insist on 30.

Sergio
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_exceptions_summary_for_SummitForge.txt (internal note)
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@summitforge.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines and SOW questions for the SummitForge connector

Thanks for the quick internal review — that helps. We reviewed Redwood's points with our legal ops and pushed back on two items we consider non-negotiable:

- Indemnity cap: SummitForge needs breach-related indemnity to be uncapped for IP infringement affecting our enterprise customers (we can provide examples where past vendor caps were inadequate).
- Subprocessors: we require written consent (not just notice) for third parties processing customer content; standard cloud infra exemptions are fine but analytics/third-party model vendors require explicit approval.

Other than those, the rest look workable; attaching an updated redline with strike/insert comments on your proposed positions (see SummitForge_Redlines_v3.pdf, updated pages 4–7). We can be flexible on payment terms (30 or 45 days) if core legal positions are accepted.

We have the 8/25 2:00pm PT window open for a call. Would appreciate Sergio on the line to discuss indemnity.

—Ethan

Ethan —

Thanks for the updated redline and for prioritizing this. Quick plan to keep us on the 8/30 target:

1) Call confirmed: 8/25 2:00pm PT — invite sent. Sergio will lead the legal discussion and I’ll run the integration/SOW points.
2) On indemnity: Sergio will present Redwood's standard cap + narrowly scoped IP carveout language during the call. We’ll ask SummitForge to provide the examples you referenced so legal can evaluate severity.
3) Subprocessors: we’ll propose a middle path — prior written consent for model vendors/analytics only, with a 10-business-day review window for Redwood to respond. Routine infra and telemetry vendors will remain on the published subprocessor list and covered by notice.
4) Follow-up deliverables: Redwood to provide a one-page exceptions log and a redline of the SOW with retention appendix by 8/27 COB.

If those sound right I’ll share the exceptions log and updated SOW redline after the call — our aim is to close commercial terms the week of 8/30.
